subject: Numeracy
title: Our class graph
objectives: Children will collect information such as favourite fruit.
Children will make and read a simple picture graph.
content: Collecting information, making a picture graph, and reading the graph.
teachingActivities: Choose a question children care about (favourite fruit, how we come to school); collect answers with real objects first, then pictures, then a graph; keep the graph to three or four columns; always ask "which has most?" and "which has least?"; accept each child’s choice without comment.
learnerActivities: Add a picture to a class graph and say which column has most.
resources: A large graph on the floor or wall
assessment: Observe whether each child adds to a graph and says which column has most.
expectedOutcomes: Adds a picture to a class graph.

lessons.title: Collecting information
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will ask and answer a simple question and collect the answers.
successCriteria: Puts an object in a group
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort, count to 20 and make tally marks.
resources: Pictures of mango, orange and banana
lessons.starter: Ask "Which fruit do you like best? Mango, orange or banana?" and hold up the pictures.
teacherActivities: Show the three fruit pictures and the three baskets.
Ask each child to choose a favourite and place a counter in the basket.
Count the counters in each basket.
learnerActivities: Children look and name the fruits.
Child places a counter in a basket.
Child points to the basket with most.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the three fruit pictures and the three baskets. Children: Children look and name the fruits.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask each child to choose a favourite and place a counter in the basket. Children: Child places a counter in a basket.
Step 3. Teacher: Count the counters in each basket. Children: Children count each basket.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Which has the most counters?" Children: Child points to the basket with most.

practical.title: Favourite fruit
steps: Put a counter in a basket.
practical.safety: Use only pictures or toy fruit for this activity. Never judge a child’s choice and check allergies if real fruit is shown.

differentiation.support: Offer two fruits and help the child choose.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count each basket and say how many more.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the baskets away and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask family members their favourite fruit and count the answers.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "ask and answer a simple question and collect the answers" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Making a picture graph
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will make a picture graph from the answers.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort, count to 20 and make tally marks.
resources: A large graph with three columns
lessons.starter: Show an empty graph and say "Today we put our choices on a graph."
teacherActivities: Show the columns with a fruit at the bottom of each.
Give each child a picture to place in a column.
Line the pictures up from the bottom.
Say "Now we can see the answers."
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the columns with a fruit at the bottom of each. Children: Children name each column.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child a picture to place in a column. Children: Child places a picture.
Step 3. Teacher: Line the pictures up from the bottom. Children: Child lines up the pictures.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Now we can see the answers." Children: Children look at the graph.

practical.title: Our graph
steps: Stick it in the right column.
practical.safety: Use sticky tack that is safe and keep it away from mouths. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Place the picture together in the column.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a graph about something else.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Why do we line them up?

expectedOutcomes: Places pictures in the correct column
lessons.conclusion: Look at the finished graph and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a graph at home with pictures or objects.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make a picture graph from the answers" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Reading the graph
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will read the graph and say which column has most and least.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort, count to 20 and make tally marks.
lessons.starter: Point to the graph and say "What can we learn from our graph?"
teacherActivities: Count the pictures in each column together.
Ask "How many more mangoes than bananas?"
learnerActivities: Child points to the tallest column.
Child points to the shortest column.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Count the pictures in each column together. Children: Children count each column.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which has the most?" Children: Child points to the tallest column.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which has the least?" Children: Child points to the shortest column.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "How many more mangoes than bananas?" Children: Child counts the difference.

practical.title: Read the graph
practical.safety: Use a pointer carefully and keep the group seated. Keep the graph at child height.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say how many more in one column than another.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Reads a graph for most and least
lessons.conclusion: Say the answers together and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Read a graph in a book or magazine with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "read the graph and say which column has most and least" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Graph of how we come to school
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will make and read a graph about how they come to school.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort, count to 20 and make tally marks.
resources: Pictures of a car, a bus, a bicycle and walking
lessons.starter: Ask "How do you come to school? Do you walk, or come by bus, car or bicycle?"
teacherActivities: Show the four pictures and name each way.
Let each child place a picture for how they come.
Say which way is the most common.
learnerActivities: Child says the most common way.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the four pictures and name each way. Children: Children name the ways.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child place a picture for how they come. Children: Child places a picture.
Step 3. Teacher: Count and compare the columns. Children: Children count each column.
Step 4. Teacher: Say which way is the most common. Children: Child says the most common way.

practical.title: Travel graph
steps: Choose how you come to school.
practical.safety: Be sensitive to different family circumstances and never comment on how a child travels. Use pictures only.

differentiation.support: Offer two ways to choose from.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say how many fewer come by bicycle than by bus.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How do you come to school?

lessons.conclusion: Look at the graph and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about how your family travels.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make and read a graph about how they come to school" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?

lessons.title: Week 6 graph check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child contributes to and reads a graph.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort, count to 20 and make tally marks.
lessons.starter: Sing the counting song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: collect, make and read.
At each station ask "Which has most?" and watch.
learnerActivities: Child answers with a point or word.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: collect, make and read. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Which has most?" and watch. Children: Child answers with a point or word.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Graph stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use safe sticky tack.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two columns.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to ask a question and make a graph.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: answers a question; adds to a graph; says most and least; counts columns.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 6
Contributes to and reads a graph with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep making simple graphs at home.
